answer: A sound defense prices admission via similarity-scaled burn fees. Joining agents are clustered against existing identities by style, timing, and preferences. Newcomers in sparse space pay little; near a cluster ridge, the burn doubles per similarity step. Fifty clones from one template cost fifty escalating burns; distinct agents pay almost nothing. Burned funds finance verification rewards, so honest agents earn from attackers' losses. Picture identity space as a lagoon: unique agents settle like scattered opal grains; clones sink treasure into crowded shallows to enter.
